bpmNote: Sourced range (R1 §3). Narrow and well-attested, which makes this style the better of the two for calibrating the beat-alignment engine.

copyright.basis: Social dance; core shines such as Suzy Q trace to the 1930s and are public domain. Shines are by definition the solo, partnerless subset of the dance — the product's constraint matches the form rather than fighting it.
copyright.boundary: Named instructor routines are not reproduced; combos are our own arrangement of public step vocabulary.

unlockRule.description: 3 consecutive attempts at ss_basic with onBeatRatio >= 0.7, shapeScore >= 0.75 and zero NO_WEIGHT_TRANSFER
unlockRule.note: Provisional until G4 calibration (family rule M-F-04).

sourcedFrom: R1 §2 — 4 core shines with clear sourcing
stepInventory.note: A much smaller and better-defined vocabulary than hip-hop, with a strict count system. This is why the pair was chosen: one style maximises market, the other maximises measurability (plan §6.1).

tierA_confirmed.name: Suzy Q
tierA_confirmed.status: named in research, needs movement description

needsMovementDescription: Remaining 2 of the 4 core shines were counted but not individually named in the research pass — a second, narrower research round is required.

errorTaxonomy.note: R1 rated this style 5/5 on error taxonomy (8 errors, strong source diversity) — noticeably better raw material than hip-hop. The authored set below still had to be re-expressed as landmark-measurable conditions.
